**0.9.0 is a breaking release.** It changes the storage and protocol format to format epoch 5 and the backup format to 5. A 0.9 node refuses epoch-4 Raft WAL directories and object-storage prefixes at startup and refuses 0.8 peers, a 0.8 node refuses 0.9 peers, and 0.9 does not restore 0.8 backups. There is no in-place upgrade, no rolling upgrade, no backup migration and no rollback.

- **If you cannot move your data yet, stay on 0.8.2.**
- **Deploy 0.9 fresh** on empty PVCs and never-used object-storage prefixes for the cold store and S3 snapshots, and give it its own `server.cluster_id`. Move the streams you keep through your applications: read them from 0.8 and write them to 0.9 over the HTTP API. A stream written again is a new stream.
- **`helm upgrade` from 0.8 stops at the first pod**, which finds the 0.8 data on its volume and exits. Recover with `helm rollback`. Keep the peer lists of 0.8 and 0.9 nodes apart.
- **Each node owns its snapshot objects.** With an S3 snapshot store, a node writes and deletes only under `<prefix>/node-<id>/`, and a follower that installs a snapshot from a peer writes its own copy first. Snapshot GC needs no grace and no clock. Delete the 0.8 snapshot prefixes once nothing reads them.
- **Raft membership names node IDs only.** Every peer address comes from `[[raft.peers]]`, and leader hints carry no address.
- **Compact MessagePack** for Raft log entries, Raft RPCs, forwarded reads and writes, WAL state files, snapshot records and backup group objects makes small appends take about half the bytes in the WAL.
- **The snapshot driver always runs.** `raft.snapshot_logs_since_last` and `storage.snapshot.drive_interval = "0s"` are refused at startup. S3 snapshot requests have their own budget (`storage.snapshot.s3_timeout`, `storage.snapshot.s3_max_retries`), and a config whose install copy cannot fit inside `raft.install_snapshot_timeout` is refused.
- **Raft runs on OpenRaft 0.10.0-alpha.37.** A leader without a live quorum refuses writes with `503 NO_LEADER`, and Raft ticks about 7 times as often.
- **Cold uploads are fenced to the leadership that made them**, and cold GC deletes only the group's own cold objects.

Known issues: [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561), and [#735](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/735), [#753](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/753) and [#754](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/754), which are new in 0.9.0. [#539](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/539), [#687](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/687), [#698](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/698) and [#709](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/709) are fixed. Every change is listed in the [0.9.0 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#090), and installing 0.9.0 is described in [Upgrading to 0.9](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#upgrading-to-09).
